title: Compact-support exchange intertwines proper ordinary counits
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum and the geometric operation datum of [def-sf-kv-maps], at $A=A_{E,n}$. Work on the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,A)$, with their specified ordinary adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ and counits $\varepsilon_u$ of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1), compact-support composition of [thm-sf-comp-composition], and the proper identifications $Ru_!\cong Ru_*$ of [prop-functor-package](3). Use the compact-support exchange of [def-exchange-projection], with the choice-independent normalization of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Let $W,U,V,V'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
 V'&\xrightarrow{\beta'}&U\\
 {\scriptstyle\alpha'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\alpha}\\
 V&\xrightarrow{\beta}&W
\end{array}
$$
be Cartesian, with all arrows separated of finite type and $\alpha$ proper (hence $\alpha'$ proper). No properness is required of $\beta$ or $\beta'$. Write
$$T:L\alpha^*R\beta_!\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Ex}_!}R\beta'_!L\alpha'^*$$
for the specified exchange, and let
$$\Theta:R\beta_!R\alpha'_*\cong R\beta_!R\alpha'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(\beta\alpha')_!=R(\alpha\beta')_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\alpha_!R\beta'_!\cong R\alpha_*R\beta'_!$$
be the specified compact-support composition comparison. For every $Z\in D^b_{ctf}(V',A)$ one has
$$\varepsilon_{\alpha,R\beta'_!Z}\circ L\alpha^*(\Theta_Z)
=R\beta'_!(\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z})\circ T_{R\alpha'_*Z}$$
as maps $L\alpha^*R\beta_!R\alpha'_*Z\longrightarrow R\beta'_!Z$. All functors, proper comparisons and composition comparisons in this equality are the named geometric ones on the stated finite-coefficient domains.

source.place: The last assertion, compatibility with composition and cancellation of the alpha-prime unit-counit pair; normalization equation (*) in the retained split

proof.text: Properness of $\alpha'$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The finite-stage preservation statements (i), (iii), (iv) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] put all the pullbacks, direct images and compact-support images used below in $D^b_{ctf}$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), each such bounded constructible finite-coefficient object admits an etale-origin witness. Choose and retain these witnesses when using compact-support composition: [thm-sf-comp-composition] is stated on that witnessed domain. Thus its domain hypothesis is satisfied, without assuming that arbitrary pro-etale complexes have etale origin.

source.place: Last assertion: domains and proper comparisons

proof.text:
Choose a compactification $\beta=pj$, with $j:V\hookrightarrow\bar V$ open and $p:\bar V\to W$ proper, using [thm-nagata-compactification]. Pull it back along $\alpha$, writing $\bar V'=U\times_W\bar V$, $a:\bar V'\to\bar V$, $p':\bar V'\to U$ and $j':V'\hookrightarrow\bar V'$. The proper/open base-change facts [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] give proper $a,p'$ and open $j'$. All schemes remain separated of finite type over $k$. Suppress canonical composition parentheses. Set $b:a^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!\alpha'^*$ and $T_p:\alpha^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*a^*$. By the defining compactification formula [def-exchange-projection], read on the compactification $(j,p)$ (equivalently, by the vertical pasting of [fix-lem-exchanges](2) for $\beta=pj$, where the formula for $(\mathrm{id},p)$ gives $T_p$ and that for $(j,\mathrm{id})$ gives $b$), and the choice independence of [fix-lem-exchanges](4),
$$T=Rp'_*(b)\circ T_pj_!.$$
Let $\chi:j_!R\alpha'_*\to Ra_*j'_!$ and $\Theta_p:Rp_*Ra_*\to R\alpha_*Rp'_*$ be the composition comparisons for the two smaller squares. Associativity of [thm-sf-comp-composition], with the proper/open normalizations of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization], identifies the specified comparison in the item with
$$\Theta=(\Theta_pj'_!)\circ Rp_*(\chi).$$
It remains to compute the ordinary mates for these two factors.

source.place: Last assertion: expand the specified compactification exchange and composition; Stacks Tags 0F7B, 0F7J

proof.text:
For the proper square, $T_p$ is the direct-image exchange of [def-exchange-projection]: the mate of the pullback-square comparison under $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ and $p'^*\dashv Rp'_*$. Take its mate instead under $\alpha^*\dashv R\alpha_*$ and $a^*\dashv Ra_*$. The resulting component is explicitly
$$C_{p,N}=R\alpha_*(Rp'_*(\varepsilon_{a,N})\circ T_{p,Ra_*N})\circ\eta_{\alpha,Rp_*Ra_*N}.$$
By the iterated-mate identity [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] (with $L_2=p'^*$, $F_1=\alpha^*$, $F_2=a^*$, $L_1=p^*$), taking these two successive mates is the conjugate of the pullback comparison $p'^*\alpha^*\cong a^*p^*$ for $pa=\alpha p'$ under the composite adjunctions $a^*p^*\dashv Rp_*Ra_*$ and $p'^*\alpha^*\dashv R\alpha_*Rp'_*$. The ordinary direct-image compositions are precisely its conjugates by [fix-prop-adjunctions](3). Clause (1) of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization] identifies that comparison with $\Theta_p$, so $C_{p,N}=\Theta_{p,N}$. Undoing the $\alpha$ adjunction, using its triangle identity, gives
$$Rp'_*(\varepsilon_{a,N})\circ T_{p,Ra_*N}
=\varepsilon_{\alpha,Rp'_*N}\circ\alpha^*\Theta_{p,N}.$$
This uses properness of $p,p',a,\alpha$, all already verified.

source.place: Last assertion: ordinary mate calculation for the proper factor

proof.text:
For the open square write $F=a^*$, $F'=\alpha'^*$, $A=Ra_*$, $A'=R\alpha'_*$, $J=j_!$, $J'=j'_!$, $Q=j^*$, $Q'=j'^*$, and let $u:1\to QJ$, $u':1\to Q'J'$ be the open units. They are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-open-closed-recollement-adjunctions]. Write $s:Q'F\cong F'Q$ for the pullback comparison. The inverse of $b:FJ\to J'F'$ is, by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], the $J'\dashv Q'$-adjunct of $s^{-1}\circ F'u$. Let $M:QA\to A'Q'$ be the ordinary square mate of $s^{-1}:F'Q\to Q'F$. The square mate of $b^{-1}:J'F'\to FJ$ under $J\dashv Q$ and $J'\dashv Q'$ is $Q'(F\varepsilon_J)\circ Q'(b^{-1}Q)\circ u'F'Q$; since $Q'b^{-1}\circ u'F'=s^{-1}J\circ F'u$ (the adjunct description above), naturality of $s$ and the triangle identity $Q\varepsilon_J\circ uQ=1$ reduce it to $s^{-1}$. Hence the iterated-mate identity [lem-trf-iterated-square-mates] (with $L_2=J'$, $F_1=F'$, $F_2=F$, $L_1=J$) shows that $M$ is the conjugate of $b^{-1}$ under $J'F'\dashv A'Q'$ and $FJ\dashv QA$. Since conjugation preserves inverse isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate],
$$(b^{-1})^c=M,\qquad b^c=M^{-1}.$$
In particular, with the notation of clause (2) of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization],
$$\lambda_Z=A'(u_Z'^{-1})\circ M_{J'Z},\qquad
\lambda_Z^{-1}=b^c_{J'Z}\circ A'(u'_Z).$$
These are formulas for the named maps, not a choice of an isomorphism between their endpoints.

source.place: Last assertion: open-factor mate and unit normalization

proof.text:
Let $C:JA'\to AJ'$ be the ordinary square mate of $b:FJ\to J'F'$. The explicit mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] is
$$C_Z=A(J'\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z})\circ A(b_{A'Z})\circ\eta_{a,JA'Z}.$$
Its open adjunct is $Q(C_Z)\circ u_{A'Z}$. Substituting this formula and the conjugate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], naturality of $u'$ and the triangle identity for $J'\dashv Q'$ give
$$Q(C_Z)\circ u_{A'Z}=b^c_{J'Z}\circ A'(u'_Z)=\lambda_Z^{-1}.$$
Explicitly, after moving $A'(u'_Z)$ through the units and $b$ by naturality, counit naturality gives $\varepsilon_{\alpha',Q'J'Z}\circ F'A'(u'_Z)=u'_Z\circ\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z}$. The open triangle then cancels $\varepsilon_{J',J'Z}\circ J'(u'_Z)=1_{J'Z}$; the remaining factors are $Q(\eta_a)$, $Q(A b)$ and $Q(AJ'\varepsilon_{\alpha'})$ preceded by $u_{A'Z}$, exactly the left side. Clause (2) of [lem-trf-compact-composition-proper-square-normalization] states that $\chi_Z$ has this same open adjunct $\lambda_Z^{-1}$. The open adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so $C_Z=\chi_Z$. Undoing the ordinary $a$ adjunction therefore yields
$$j'_!(\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z})\circ b_{R\alpha'_*Z}
=\varepsilon_{a,j'_!Z}\circ a^*(\chi_Z).$$

source.place: Last assertion: identify the open-factor mate with the specified proper/open composition

proof.text:
Now compute the right side of the required equality using the factorizations in step 2. The open-factor identity of step 5, naturality of $T_p$ for $\chi_Z$, and the proper-factor identity of step 3, in that order, give
$$\begin{aligned}
R\beta'_!(\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z})\circ T_{R\alpha'_*Z}
&=Rp'_*(j'_!\varepsilon_{\alpha',Z}\circ b_{R\alpha'_*Z})\circ T_{p,j_!R\alpha'_*Z}\\
&=Rp'_*(\varepsilon_{a,j'_!Z})\circ Rp'_*a^*(\chi_Z)\circ T_{p,j_!R\alpha'_*Z}\\
&=Rp'_*(\varepsilon_{a,j'_!Z})\circ T_{p,Ra_*j'_!Z}\circ\alpha^*Rp_*(\chi_Z)\\
&=\varepsilon_{\alpha,Rp'_*j'_!Z}\circ\alpha^*(\Theta_{p,j'_!Z})\circ\alpha^*Rp_*(\chi_Z)\\
&=\varepsilon_{\alpha,R\beta'_!Z}\circ\alpha^*(\Theta_Z).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the compactification identifications are the ones of [def-exchange-projection], and [fix-lem-exchanges](4) and [thm-sf-comp-composition] make them independent of the chosen compactification and associative. The counit is the specified ordinary counit of [fix-prop-adjunctions](1). Thus the calculation proves the equality with the exact comparisons in the statement. No properness of $\beta$ or $\beta'$ entered.

split_report.summary: Retained the statement and previous search records; repaired an unsupported exceptional-to-ordinary mate inference. The six-step proof checks finite-coefficient etale-origin domains, factors beta into open and proper maps, uses the existing proper/open composition normalization node, computes both ordinary mates, and pastes the resulting counit identities explicitly. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the compact-support exchange/composition compatibility asserted in the last paragraph for the last assertion of lem-trf-trace-map-exchange.proof.md, with its omitted normalization calculation expanded. The sentence Ex_!=Ex_* based only on alpha proper has the wrong direction: beta need not be proper. We retain compact supports and use the prescribed geometric compactification instead; the unit route and item statement are unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Choice independence and pasting of the named compact-support exchange, retaining the unit route.

Its cross-unit statement is used as a generic normalization tool for the proper/proper and proper/open compactification composition maps; the sk-p-proper route does not prove this compactification normalization itself.
